source.title: Demystifying Batch Normalization in ReLU Networks: Equivalent Convex Optimization Models and Implicit Regularization
source.authors: Tolga Ergen; Arda Sahiner; Batu Mehmet Ozturkler; J. Pauly; Morteza Mardani; Mert Pilanci

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent cutoff or garbling that prevents reading the relevant sections.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares standard batch-normalized ReLU networks with equivalent whitened formulations and measures training and test performance, providing conceptual evidence about optimizer-dependent generalization and batch-size effects.
record.gate_note: Reports its own training/test results for BN and whitened models, truncated variants, batch-size ablations, and a non-BN comparison. Batch sizes and optimizer settings are tested, but random-label memorization, width past interpolation, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, and removal of memorized examples are not tested. Figure-only curves are not converted into precise values; cited findings are not rows.
record.test_reason: Appendix A.4 explicitly reports that the CIFAR-10 CNN achieves higher test accuracy than the paper's fully connected networks, bearing on V3 in a new BN setting. The batch-size experiments use roughly matched elapsed time rather than fixed epochs, so they do not test V5's specified budget condition.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate for the empirical conclusions: GD on standard BN networks favors high singular-value directions, and explicit singular-value truncation can match or improve generalization. The paper also establishes equivalent convex formulations and closed-form optima in specified regimes.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies weight-decay-regularized ReLU networks with batch normalization, comparing standard non-convex models with equivalent whitened convex formulations and singular-value truncation. It does not use the original studies' interventions for the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size is varied in BN models; authors report roughly equivalent train and test performance. Singular-value truncation level changes performance, with low values underfitting and high values overfitting in CNAE-9. Optimizer (SGD versus Adam), dataset, learning rate, architecture, and training duration are also varied across experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: Batch sizes 50–1000 give roughly equivalent CNN performance, and smaller batches do not improve the two-layer BN results, under elapsed-time comparisons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In these BN experiments, smaller batches offer no reported generalization advantage when training time is roughly matched.

fits_no_version.finding: Standard BN and equivalent whitened formulations generalize differently under SGD.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SGD on the standard BN parameterization preferentially learns high singular-value directions and generalizes better than SGD on its equivalent whitened parameterization.

fits_no_version.finding: Singular-value truncation can recover or improve generalization, with excessive truncation underfitting and insufficient truncation overfitting.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Filtering low singular-value directions can make the tested convex BN formulations match or outperform standard BN networks, depending on dataset and truncation level.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding BN improves the reported fully connected network comparisons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: BN improves test performance of the tested two-layer fully connected networks on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100.

record.problems: The relevant performance curves in several figures lack exact numerical values in the text. Experiments vary in training duration, selected learning rates, datasets, and architectures. Batch-size findings are described as roughly equivalent, without numerical uncertainty estimates. The main benchmark experiments select learning rates based on test performance.
record.rows_left_out: No results were omitted due to the 60-row limit. Cited prior work in the related-work section is not recorded as rows. The SGD/Adam curve comparisons among standard, convex, and truncated forms are included only where the text states a result; detailed learning-rate curves and extended training curves are otherwise not separately extracted.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting paired with natural-label and random-label held-out accuracy.
Widening beyond zero training error and its effect on test error.
The contribution of local connectivity, learned sparse connections, convolution-derived initialization, and a comparison controlling optimizer and training recipe.
Adaptive-versus-SGD held-out performance under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size penalties under fixed epoch budgets and recovery through recipe adaptations; the reported batch comparisons instead roughly match elapsed time.
Dropout interventions and their dependence on data size, dropout strength, or augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps.
Removing highly memorized examples versus random removal.

missing.what: Record the explicit CNN-versus-fully-connected comparison: CNN test accuracy is 67.06%, and the authors state that it exceeds their fully connected results. Identify the Figure 3 fully connected comparator and retain the differing optimizer, width, and training budget; its precise accuracy cannot be recovered from the supplied text.
missing.locator: Appendix A.4, paragraph following Table 1; Figure 3; Appendix A.7

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V3. Its cross-architecture result supports the observed CNN advantage only in the reported setting. Equal-time batch-size findings cannot establish absence of a fixed-epoch large-batch penalty. Figure curves in the supplied text do not permit precise numerical extraction.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence are not tested.
No width sweep around the interpolation threshold or test-error double-descent measurement.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks addressing local connectivity as the cause of an advantage; the reported CNN comparison is between BN and convex variants of a CNN.
No adaptive-optimizer versus SGD generalization comparison on the same model and task. Adam is used to compare BN and whitened/truncated formulations.

The study tests batch-size effects on BN models and reports roughly equivalent performance; it does not test the claim that large batches hurt under fixed epoch budgets across image classifiers and language models, or the proposed recipe adaptations.
Dropout is not added or removed in the reported experiments.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or competing generalization measures are evaluated.
No memorized examples are identified, removed, or compared with random removals.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10: the standard two-layer BN CNN compared with the paper's fully connected networks, using separately configured training recipes.
relationships.reason: R11 reports 67.06% CNN test accuracy; Appendix A.4 explicitly states that CNN accuracy exceeds the reported fully connected results. This verdict uses that textual comparison; optimizer and budget differences prevent attributing the advantage specifically to local connectivity.
relationships.display_finding: The reported higher CNN test accuracy remains unverified across separately configured optimizers and training budgets.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
